_comment: REAL — recorded from seestar-mcp's get_run_state (main @ d555c4b).
This machine happened to hold a run_state.json left by their end-to-end
verification run, so the recording caught the UNKNOWN state rather than the
commoner idle one — a stamp older than the 15-minute window, with the run
That is the case worth having recorded, because it contradicts the shorthand
in the note announcing the tool ('run: null when idle'): `unknown` carries a
run object. A consumer that reads `run` as proof of a live session would be
wrong here, which is exactly the confident-wrong-answer the tri-state exists
to prevent. Idle and active are in fixtures/synthetic/.
Also visible here and not in the note: slot_ends_utc and park_deadline_utc
are present-and-null, while targets_remaining and notes are OMITTED. Those
are different states and the schema treats them differently.
